technical.prompt: What is the margin period of risk?
expectedPoints: Time to close out a defaulter's positions

choices.answer: The time needed to close out a defaulter's positions
distractors: The time a member has to pay its fees
The length of a trading session
The life of a futures contract

technical.prompt: What is a margin model based on value at risk?
expectedPoints: Estimates potential loss at a confidence level
Over the margin period of risk

choices.answer: A model estimating likely worst losses to set initial margin
distractors: A model setting exchange trading fees
A model ranking members by size

technical.prompt: What is a scenario-based margin approach?
expectedPoints: Revalues portfolio under price and volatility shifts

choices.answer: Revaluing a portfolio under set shocks
distractors: Charging a flat fee on every trade
Asking members to guess their losses

technical.prompt: What is a collateral haircut?

choices.answer: A discount on collateral's value for price risk
distractors: A fee for storing members' collateral
A cut in clearing members' pay
A rule limiting the size of trades

technical.prompt: What types of collateral do CCPs usually accept?

choices.answer: Cash and high-quality bonds
distractors: Any asset the member happens to own
Shares in the clearing house itself

technical.prompt: What is the Cover 2 standard?
expectedPoints: Prefunded resources cover the default of the two members, with their affiliates, that would cause the largest combined exposure
Measured under extreme but plausible market conditions
Expected of CCPs with complex risk profiles or systemic importance in several jurisdictions; others may meet Cover 1
Set by the international principles for financial market infrastructures

choices.answer: Covering defaults of the two largest exposures
distractors: Two clearing houses covering each other's losses
Margin covering two days of price moves
Insurance covering two products per member

technical.prompt: What are assessment rights?
expectedPoints: CCP can call more funds from surviving members

choices.answer: A right to call more funds from surviving members
distractors: Members' right to assess the CCP's staff
A regulator's right to fine members
A member's right to inspect trades

technical.prompt: What is client clearing?
expectedPoints: Clearing members clear trades for clients
Clients post margin to the member

choices.answer: Members clearing trades on behalf of their clients
distractors: Clients clearing their own accounts directly

technical.prompt: What is the difference between omnibus and individual segregation?

choices.answer: Omnibus pools clients' assets; individual keeps each separate
distractors: Individual pools assets; omnibus keeps them separate

technical.prompt: What is porting?
expectedPoints: Moving client positions to another member

choices.answer: Moving clients' positions to a new member after a default

technical.prompt: What is real-time gross settlement?

choices.answer: Settling each payment individually and immediately
distractors: Settling all payments once a week
Netting all payments at day end

technical.prompt: What is deferred net settlement?

choices.answer: Netting payments and settling balances at set times
distractors: Settling all payments only in gold

technical.prompt: Why does settling in central bank money matter?
expectedPoints: No credit risk on the settlement asset
Commercial bank money carries bank risk

choices.answer: Central bank money carries no bank credit risk
distractors: It is always faster than other money

technical.prompt: What is trade affirmation?

choices.answer: Confirming trade details before settlement
distractors: Praising a trader for a good trade
Reporting a trade to tax authorities

technical.prompt: What are standing settlement instructions?

choices.answer: Pre-agreed account details used to settle trades
distractors: Rules for standing on a trading floor

technical.prompt: What is partial settlement?
expectedPoints: Settling the available portion of a trade

choices.answer: Settling the part of a trade that's available now

technical.prompt: What is wrong-way risk in clearing?
expectedPoints: Exposure rises as member's credit worsens
Such as posting own bonds as collateral

choices.answer: Exposure that grows as the member weakens
distractors: Risk of trading in the wrong direction
Risk of paying the wrong bank

technical.prompt: What is CCP liquidity risk?
expectedPoints: Needing cash to pay obligations on time
Relies on liquid collateral and credit lines

choices.answer: The risk the CCP can't pay what it owes on time
distractors: The risk members trade too little
The risk CCP shares are illiquid
The risk of low trading fees

technical.prompt: Why do CCPs add concentration add-ons to margin?

choices.answer: Large positions take longer to close out
